authorship: AI-authored analytical review; not human verified.

source_identity.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations

scope: All 22 canonical records: 17 taxonomy definitions and five cross-cutting threat-model, mitigation, benchmark or evaluation propositions. Review is limited to these represented propositions; it is not a complete extraction of the report.
excluded_material: Unrepresented examples, references and explanatory repetition were not promoted into new EXTREQ records.
No attack definition was treated as an independent governance duty.
No Fidelity Class relationships, Incident findings or new taxonomy categories were created.
unresolved_issues: The report expressly describes evolving attacks and mitigations, trade-offs and context-dependent risk; no universal control claim was inferred.
AI review is not human verification; assurance is limited to the represented extraction scope.

entries.source_comparison: Section 3.4.3, printed page 53 / NISTAML.039 describes privacy exfiltration through prompt injection into systems with restricted-resource access, not generic compromise of all tools or external systems.
entries.reverse_coverage_rationale: Attack taxonomy definition; it describes a threat mechanism rather than imposing a neutral governance invariant.
entries.current_summary: Connected-resource compromise uses prompt injection to cause a generative AI system to leak private information from restricted resources it can access.
